source.title: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms.
source.location: Fig. 2A legend (morphometric n per head-shape group, pseudo groups); Results 2.1 and 2.2 text; Methods 4.1

stage: trunk fragment (pre-tail fragment, cut posterior to pharynx and anterior to tail)
injury: amputation posterior to the pharynx and anterior to the tail (pre-tail fragment)

intervention.duration: 3 days in octanol, then water until scoring
intervention.description: Pre-tail fragments amputated and immediately soaked in octanol for 3 days, then kept in water to finish regeneration.

readout.method: visual head-shape classification and geometric morphometrics of head landmarks

notes: Counts are the morphometric subsample from the Fig. 2A legend, not the full treated cohort (the text and Fig 1/3 legends give n>243 treated fragments, but no breakdown of that cohort in text). normal = pseudo G. dorotocephala head (n=7). altered_shape = pseudo D. japonica-like (n=13), pseudo P. felina-like (n=5) and pseudo S. mediterranea-like (n=6), summed to 24. Breakdown of the full cohort (Fig 3B bars) could not be read from the text and is not used. n_total is 31 to match the counts; the full cohort is >243.

source.title: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms.
source.location: Fig. 2A legend (WT G. dorotocephala 10 days after amputation and regenerated in water); Results 2.1 text (control condition)

stage: trunk fragment (pre-tail fragment, cut posterior to pharynx and anterior to tail)
injury: amputation posterior to the pharynx and anterior to the tail (pre-tail fragment)

intervention.description: Pre-tail fragments amputated and kept in water for 10 days with no drug treatment.

readout.method: visual head-shape classification and geometric morphometrics of head landmarks

notes: n=8 from the Fig. 2A legend (WT G. dorotocephala regenerated in water 10 days). Text states that the normal regeneration control had 100% fidelity to the species-specific head shape (cites Fig S1A); the supplement was not available to check its n, so the n=8 morphometric group is used as the count. No variant head shapes were reported in this control.

source.title: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms.
source.location: Fig. 6I legend (pseudo morphologies remodeled back to WT GD after 30 days; n=6 remodeled worms); Results 2.7 text

stage: trunk fragment (pre-tail fragment, cut posterior to pharynx and anterior to tail)
injury: amputation posterior to the pharynx and anterior to the tail (pre-tail fragment)

intervention.duration: 3 days in octanol, then water until day 30
intervention.description: Pre-tail fragments amputated and immediately soaked in octanol for 3 days, then kept in water and followed to day 30 after amputation.

readout.method: daily photographs of head shape in water, scored by visual head-shape classification

notes: Fig. 6I legend lists 6 remodeled worms (pink group) that had remodeled from the pseudo head shapes back to wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape by day 30. Counts are the remodeled subgroup only, not the full octanol cohort. The remodeled group is a subset of the octanol-treated pseudo worms; the number of pseudo worms that were followed up to day 30 is not stated separately.
